title: The Artin–Schreier sheaf is a lisse character sheaf
statement:
Fix the Fourier datum of [sk-def-fourier-set]: distinct primes $p,\ell$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ with $q=p^r$ and $r\ge1$, its algebraic closure $k$, and adic coefficients $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ formed at a finite stage $E$ containing $\mu_p$. Fix the nontrivial character $\Psi:\mathbf F_p\to E^\times$ and $\psi=\Psi\circ\operatorname{Tr}_{k_0/\mathbf F_p}$ of [def-fd-additive-character]. This is the specialization $F'=E$ of that definition: $\operatorname{char}E=0\ne p$ and $E(\mu_p)=E$ since $\mu_p\subset E$. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme and $f,g\in\Gamma(X_0,\mathcal O_{X_0})$. In the following, $\pi:Y\to X_0$ denotes the auxiliary prime-degree cover $Y=\operatorname{Spec}_{X_0}(\mathcal O_{X_0}[T]/(T^p-T-f))$, with $\sigma_a(T)=T+a$. The notation $\mathcal L_{\psi,f}$ retains the current degree-$q$ definition of [sk-def-as]; its identification with the $\Psi$-summand of this prime-degree cover is part of the argument below. In connected-case assertions, connected includes nonemptiness. The pushforward and cohomology below mean adic realizations of the compatible finite coefficient systems, not discrete non-torsion etale sheaves. For the cohomology formula $i\ge0$ and $a\in k_0$, write $\mathcal L_{\psi_a}=\mathcal L_{\psi,ax}$, including $a=0$. Geometric Frobenius uses [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace].

$\pi$ is finite étale of degree $p$, and the translations $\sigma_a$
($a\in\Fp$) act simply transitively on its geometric fibres: they make $Y$
an $\Fp$-torsor over $X_0$. The automorphisms of $Y$ *as an
$\Fp$-torsor* (those commuting with the $\sigma_a$) form $\Gamma(X_0,\Fp)$,
which is $\Fp$ when $X_0$ is connected; and $\Fp\to\operatorname{Aut}(Y/X_0)$
is an isomorphism when $Y$ is connected, but not in general (for $f=0$ the
cover $Y=\coprod_{a\in\Fp}X_0$ is split, and e.g. for $p=3$,
$X_0=\Spec\mathbf F_3$ its full automorphism group over $X_0$ is $S_3$).
Over $\Aone_{k_0}$ the covering is $y\mapsto x=y^p-y$. Its pushforward
decomposes as
$\pi_*\Qlb\cong\bigoplus_{\chi\in\widehat{\Fp}}\mathcal L_\chi$ with each
$\mathcal L_\chi$ lisse of rank one and $\mathcal L_0=1$ (for $\chi\ne0$,
$\mathcal L_\chi$ may or may not be constant, e.g. all are constant when $f=0$);
consequently $\mathcal L_{\psi,f}$ is lisse of rank one,

$$
\mathcal L_{\psi,f}\otimes\mathcal L_{\psi,g}\cong\mathcal L_{\psi,f+g},
\qquad
(\mathcal L_{\psi,f})^{-1}\cong\mathcal L_{\psi,-f}.
$$

At a closed point $u$ the geometric Frobenius acts on $\mathcal L_{\psi,f}$ by
$\Psi(\Tr_{\kappa(u)/\Fp}f(u))=\psi(\Tr_{\kappa(u)/k_0}f(u))$; so its trace
function on $\Aone_{k_0}$ is
$t_{\mathcal L_{\psi,ax}}(u)=\psi(\Tr_{\kappa(u)/k_0}(au))$; and
$H^q(\Aone_{\bar k},\mathcal L_{\psi_a})=0$ for $(q,a)\neq(0,0)$, while
$H^0(\Aone_{\bar k},\Qlb)=\Qlb$ and $H^q(\Aone_{\bar k},\Qlb)=0$ for $q>0$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-fd-as-cover] to the explicitly specified prime-degree cover $Y_f=\operatorname{Spec}_{X_0}\mathcal O_{X_0}[T]/(T^p-T-f)$. Its statement gives finite etaleness of degree $p$, simple transitivity of the translations, the torsor automorphism group $\Gamma(X_0,\mathbf F_p)$, and the full automorphism group when $Y_f$ is nonempty and connected. If $X_0$ is nonempty and connected, a locally constant map $X_0\to\mathbf F_p$ has a single value, so $\Gamma(X_0,\mathbf F_p)=\mathbf F_p$. The same cited statement includes the split-cover counterexample: for $f=0$ and $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_3$, all permutations of the three components are allowed, giving $S_3$. These claims concern $Y_f$, not the distinct degree-$q$ cover defining $\mathcal L_{\psi,f}$ in [sk-def-as].

source.place: First paragraph: prime-degree cover and automorphisms

proof.text: For $X_0=\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ and $f=x$, [lem-fd-as-cover-affine-line] identifies $Y_f$ with $\mathbf A^1_{k_0,y}$ and the map with $x=y^p-y$. Apply [lem-fd-as-characters] to this cover, or to $Y_f$ for general $f$: it gives the decomposition indexed by $\widehat{\mathbf F}_p$, rank one of every summand, and the constant invariant summand. Its explicit $f=0$ clause rules out any assertion that a nontrivial character necessarily gives a nonconstant sheaf.

source.place: First paragraph: affine-line presentation and isotypic decomposition

proof.text: Interpret these finite-monodromy sheaves in the adic sense of [sk-def-fourier-set]. Choose its $E$ containing $\mu_p$, put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$, and start with the constant free rank-one $A_n$ system on $Y_f$. By [lem-fd-finite-etale-adic-cohomology], its finite direct images and their base changes are the compatible systems realizing the adic direct image. Each projector $p^{-1}\sum_b\chi(-b)\sigma_b^*$ is defined over $\mathcal O_E$: roots of unity and $p$ are units. On the torsor trivialization its image consists of functions $h(b)=\chi(b)c$, so evaluation at $0$ identifies that image with $A_n$. These descriptions commute with $A_{n+1}\to A_n$. Thus the summands and the splitting maps of Step 2 are compatible finite free systems; their completed, rationalized and common-stage realizations give precisely the asserted adic decomposition. No torsion-only cohomology theorem is applied to a discrete rational sheaf.

source.place: Isotypic decomposition, with the standing adic coefficient convention

proof.text: The imported unit uses two covers without distinguishing them. To compare them faithfully, write $q=p^r$ and use [lem-a1-artin-schreier-trace-cover-map] with auxiliary $b=1$. Its map $\theta:Y_q\to Y_f$ is $t=\Theta(y)=\sum_{i<r}y^{p^i}$, satisfies $\theta(y+c)=\theta(y)+\operatorname{Tr}_{k_0/\mathbf F_p}(c)$, and is the quotient on each geometric fibre by $H=\ker\operatorname{Tr}$. It also commutes with base change. Specialize [def-fd-additive-character] to $F'=E$: its characteristic is $0\ne p$, and $E(\mu_p)=E$ by the standing coefficient assumption. Hence its fixed $\Psi$ is our $E$-valued character and $\psi(c)=\Psi(\operatorname{Tr}(c))$. Use [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split] on the two finite etale covers to work locally with their constant finite sets. Pullback of functions along $\theta$ sends a $\Psi$-eigenfunction on the prime-degree torsor to a $\psi$-eigenfunction on the degree-$q$ torsor. Conversely such a function is constant on $H$-orbits, hence descends uniquely along $\theta$; its descended translation character is $\Psi$. These maps are inverse, commute with coefficient quotients, and are defined over $k_0$.

source.place: Degree-p presentation versus the current AS_q definition; finite-set character comparison

proof.text: Apply the exchange and coefficient-compatibility clauses of [lem-fd-finite-etale-adic-cohomology] to the two covers in Step 4. They identify pullback of the universal character projectors with the projectors of the covers of $f$. The inverse maps of Step 4 therefore realize an isomorphism between the prime-degree $\Psi$-summand and the current $\mathcal L_{\psi,f}$ of [sk-def-as], at every finite level and then at the adic common stage. Their definition over $k_0$ retains the canonical Weil structures. The hypotheses hold: all schemes are separated of finite type over a field, hence noetherian and finite-dimensional, and $\ell\ne p$ is invertible. The sheaf $\mathcal L_{\psi,f}$ in the statements of [lem-fd-as-characters] and [lem-fd-as-lisse] is the prime-degree $\Psi$-summand $e_\Psi\cdot\pi_*\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of [def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf], i.e. the source of this isomorphism, for $f$, $g$, $f+g$ and $-f$ alike. Transported along it, [lem-fd-as-lisse] gives lissity of rank one, $\mathcal L_{\psi,f}\otimes\mathcal L_{\psi,g}\simeq\mathcal L_{\psi,f+g}$, and inverse $\mathcal L_{\psi,-f}$. This is the cited character-sheaf identity, not an inference that an arbitrary torsor has a group law.

source.place: Lisse rank one, tensor product, and inverse; current-definition identification

proof.text: Let $u$ be a closed point of $X_0$ of degree $n$, choose its geometric point $\bar u$, and let $z=f(u)\in\mathbf F_{q^n}$. Put $M=\mathcal L_{\psi,x}$ on the geometric line, with its canonical Weil map $\theta$. By [sk-def-as], $\mathcal L_{\psi,f}=Lf^*M$. The pullback-composition isomorphism [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition], rationalized as prescribed by [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], identifies $L\bar u^*Lf^*M$ with $L(f\bar u)^*M$. Because $f$ is defined over $k_0$, $f g_X=g_{\mathbf A^1}f$. The equivariant composition comparisons in [lem-fix-weil-operations] therefore identify the $n$-fold pulled-back Weil map with $Lf^*(\theta^{[n]})$. Under the displayed point-complex identification, naturality of the point transport [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural] identifies $I^{[n]}$ on the two sides. Inserting these two identifications into the three-arrow definition of $F_u$ in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] gives exactly $F_z^{(n)}$. In particular one uses the $n$-fold operator at $z$, even if the closed-point degree of $z$ divides $n$ properly.

source.place: Trace clause: pullback of the local operator from the coordinate sheaf

proof.text: Apply the rational-point formula of [lem-fd-as-trace] with its nonzero parameter $a=1$ to $z\in\mathbf A^1(\mathbf F_{q^n})$. Its sheaf $\mathcal L_{\psi,x}$ is that of [def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf], the $\Psi$-summand of the prime-degree cover $T^p-T=x$; Steps 4–5 with $X_0=\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ and $f=x$ identify it with $M$ by an isomorphism defined over $k_0$, hence compatible with the Weil maps, and an isomorphism of Weil pairs preserves the local operators and their traces. It gives $\operatorname{Tr}(F_z^{(n)}\mid M_{\bar z})=\psi(\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbf F_{q^n}/k_0}z)$. Step 5 makes the point complex one-dimensional in degree zero, so its trace is the scalar by which its operator acts. Step 6 now gives the asserted scalar at $u$ for arbitrary $f$, including $f(u)=0$. For the second expression, use [lem-a1-finite-field-trace-frobenius-sum] on $\kappa(u)/k_0$, $k_0/\mathbf F_p$ and $\kappa(u)/\mathbf F_p$: the iterated sum is $\sum_{j<n}\sum_{i<r}z^{p^{rj+i}}=\sum_{m<rn}z^{p^m}$. Together with the $F'=E$ specialization of [def-fd-additive-character] checked in Step 4, this proves $\psi(\operatorname{Tr}_{\kappa(u)/k_0}z)=\Psi(\operatorname{Tr}_{\kappa(u)/\mathbf F_p}z)$. Substituting $f=ax$ proves the linear trace formula for every $a\in k_0$, including $a=0$.

source.place: Trace clause: apply the coordinate calculation and expand trace transitivity

proof.text: Apply [lem-fd-cohomology-affine-line-character] with its finite field $k=k_0$, its algebraic closure $K=\bar k_0$, and the fixed nontrivial prime-field character $\Psi$. Its statement expressly uses the prime-degree summand, not a discrete rational cohomology group. Steps 4–5 identify that sheaf for $f=ax$ with the current $\mathcal L_{\psi,ax}$. Its displayed formula gives vanishing for $(i,a)\ne(0,0)$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ when $(i,a)=(0,0)$. Finally [lem-fd-affine-line-constant-cohomology] gives the separate constant-coefficient assertion, including the isomorphism in degree zero induced by constant sections. These are ordinary adic cohomology groups in all degrees $i\ge0$.

source.place: Final paragraph: nontrivial affine-line character cohomology and constant case
